AGENTS.md

Source: AGENTS.md

Project instructions for AI coding agents. AGENTS.md-aware tools read this file directly. It records only what the code, DESCRIPTION, Makefile, and configuration files do not already make clear; read those for the rest.

Package overview

statsExpressions creates tidy data frames and plotmath expressions with details from statistical tests. It is the statistical backend for ggstatsplot, which consumes the returned columns and attributes, so keep them stable.

Implementation patterns

  • Supported type values vary by function, and some functions, such as pairwise_contingency_table(), take no type. Normalise type with extract_stats_type(), then follow the function’s existing branching rather than imposing one shared switch() shape.
  • Normalise easystats output with tidy_model_parameters() and tidy_model_effectsize() instead of renaming columns or rebuilding confidence intervals by hand.
  • Inside mutate() and other data-masking calls, including glue() called there, a bare name resolves to a column of data before a local variable. Build local values such as expression templates before the call and refer to them with .env$name, so input columns can’t shadow them.
  • Preserve tidy evaluation for unquoted column arguments, and use the base pipe (|>).

Validation

Start with the narrowest check that proves a change, such as the affected testthat files and snapshots. When a change affects shared behaviour, dependencies, generated metadata, or workflows, also run the full gate:

air format . --check
make lint
make hooks
make check

Testing

  • Snapshot the output instead of hand-writing expected values, with the tidy columns and the expression column as separate snapshots:

    test_that("descriptive name", {
  df <- function_under_test(data = dataset, x = var1, y = var2)
  expect_snapshot(dplyr::select(df, -expression))
  expect_snapshot(df[["expression"]])
})

  • Cover input combinations with patrick::with_parameters_test_that(), naming cases in a .test_name column (test_name is deprecated).

  • Codecov requires 100% project and patch coverage.

  • Set seeds only before Bayesian or otherwise stochastic tests.

  • Use skip_if_not_installed() for optional dependencies, and suppress warnings only when a test deliberately exercises a warning path.

Documentation

  • Never edit generated files by hand. After changing roxygen comments or README.Rmd, run make document and commit the regenerated NAMESPACE, man/*.Rd, and README.md.
  • Shared prose and tables live in man/rmd-fragments/, and shared example code in man/examples/. They feed the Rd files, README.Rmd, and the vignettes, so edit the source rather than a rendered copy.
  • Keep the README introductory and link to articles for method tables and output schemas. Add examples only for a distinct workflow or important behaviour, not for every function or option.
  • Use sentence case for prose headings, preserving function names, proper nouns, and published titles. Keep table labels such as Hypothesis testing and Effect size estimation bold.
  • End each vignette with a Citation section calling citation("statsExpressions"). Write the footer inline: pkgdown can render a vignette from a temporary file, which breaks relative child documents.
  • @examplesIf cannot wrap an @example file. For a NOT_CRAN guard around a shared example file, copy the \dontshow{if (...) withAutoprint(\{ # examplesIf} and \dontshow{\}) # examplesIf} lines from R/two-sample-test.R. This is the intended form, not a compatibility fallback: it keeps auto-printing, and pkgdown recognises the # examplesIf markers.

Versioning and changelog

  • Development versions use a fourth-component .9000 suffix. Keep the version in DESCRIPTION, codemeta.json, and the first NEWS.md heading in sync.
  • Keep NEWS.md concise and user-facing. Record behaviour and compatibility changes, including a higher minimum R version, a newly required package, or a dependency minimum that new code requires. Omit routine dependency updates and lint, formatting, CI, or generated-file maintenance.

Repository skills

Task-specific procedures live in .agents/skills/. Read one only when the task matches it:

  • create-release: prepare, submit, resume, or publish a CRAN release.
  • update-dependencies: update dependencies, change the minimum R version, or add, remove, or move a dependency.
  • maintain-ci: change or debug workflows under .github/workflows/.

User-invoked prompts live in .github/prompts/. Keep each topic in exactly one place: AGENTS.md for every-session rules, a skill or prompt for task-specific procedures.

Continuous integration

Workflows under .github/workflows/ are thin callers of shared reusable workflows; the maintain-ci skill covers changing them.

  • Reference IndrajeetPatil/workflows reusable workflows as @main, never a commit SHA. The owner maintains them and is the only person who can contribute to this repository, so there is no external-contributor risk, and @main keeps it on the latest version. Code scanners (CodeQL actions/unpinned-tag, zizmor unpinned-uses) flag this by design: do not report it or propose a pin; dismiss such alerts as “won’t fix” with this reason.

Benchmarks

See benchmarks/README.md for API coverage policy, workload catalogue, local execution, and interpretation of CodSpeed results.

Pull requests

Open pull requests as ready for review. After pushing, wait for CI and fix any failures, then get Codex approval on the current head before squash-merging.
